```{r setup}
library(PhenotypeR)
```

## Define diagnostics

`newPhenotypeRSpecifications()` stores the settings for each diagnostic. Supply
one named list for a single configuration or a list of named lists for several
configurations.

```{r}
specifications <- newPhenotypeRSpecifications(
  populationDiagnostics = list(
    cohortId = "my_cohort",
    incidence = TRUE,
    periodPrevalence = TRUE,
    populationSample = 100000,
    populationDateRange = as.Date(c("2015-01-01", "2020-12-31"))
  )
)

specifications
```

Use `NA` for an open date range endpoint. The spreadsheet and JSON formats
represent a date range as `YYYY-MM-DD to YYYY-MM-DD`, for example
`2015-01-01 to 2020-12-31` or `NA to 2020-12-31`. Imported ranges are checked
as ISO dates; they are not evaluated as R code.

## Export and import

Specifications can be exported to and imported from Excel or JSON. The
`as_tibble()` representation can also be used to review the rows before export.

```{r, eval = FALSE}
dplyr::as_tibble(specifications)

exportPhenotypeRSpecifications(
  specifications,
  fileName = "my_specifications",
  path = tempdir(),
  type = "excel"
)

importPhenotypeRSpecifications(
  file.path(tempdir(), "my_specifications.xlsx")
)
```
